pr_title: Make pausing on window focus loss instantaneous
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/11624 as per https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/11624#issuecomment-770118396

I've moved the "pause on focus lost" logic outside of the button and into `Player` while at it, given that the button is no longer relevant in pausing for this case.

I've also corrected `IsBreakTime` to become `true` by default, and calculate its value directly in the property to avoid incorrectly setting it to `false` there.

Cannot add a test case (unfortunately) for the above issue as there's no window in a headless host.
pr_comments: Haven't checked the code, but this doesn't seem to work correctly if you make the window inactive too soon after the last pause.
I guess this isn't a regression and also happens on master if you set your hold-to-pause time way down.

issue_context.title: Unpausing the game does not require you to put your cursor where it was if the game was paused via tabbing out
issue_context.body:
As the title says, when the game pauses due to tabbing out (alt tabbing or another program stealing focus) the game does not require you to go through the process of putting your cursor back where it was, like you normally would. I think part of the problem is that it does not pause immediately as I was actually able to tab out and back in once without it pausing.

Video [here](https://youtu.be/jZPvDh7RDfA) of me demonstrating. The black screen is me tabbing out, it takes a second for OBS to re-focus on osu! after tabbing back in.

osu! lazer 2021.129.0

I don't really think they will be helpful, but here are my logs:

[network.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/5892300/network.log)
[performance.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/5892301/performance.log)
[runtime.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/5892302/runtime.log)
[updater.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/5892297/updater.log)
[database.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/5892298/database.log)
comments: Are you able to upload the video directly to github (or somewhere apart from youtube)? I can't view it due to copyright issues. Alternatively, upload without an audio track.
Sorry about that. [Here's](https://youtu.be/fWwlGnp2XuQ) a version with no audio and no copyright claim on youtube.
Can reproduce as well, will investigate through.

This is happening because of the hold delay between "user focusing out of the game" and "the player pausing", making the gameplay cursor hide before the player is paused, which causes `LastFrameState` to be `Hidden`, and therefore not show the resume overlay, due to the conditions in there (`LastFrameState == Visible` for avoiding showing resume overlay when the pause is done by the user manually moving to the hold-for-menu button, in which case the gameplay cursor will become hidden):https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/1793385e96270a9b07050845b37b14fde04fe5c5/osu.Game/Rulesets/UI/DrawableRuleset.cs#L217-L224

There are two ways to fix this, either:
 1. not apply the hold delay to pausing on cases like alt-tabbing
 2. or not let the game cursor hide when alt-tabbing. 

not sure what fix to apply, I would personally go with (1) as it feels incorrect to delay it, but that's just my opinion.

I would say the second is the correct resolution? There's no reason the gameplay cursor should become hidden when the window focus is lost (I'm not even sure how this would be happening). It should be exclusively managed by the gameplay logic.

For reason why, it's because when the window focus is lost, all hovered drawables become unhovered, causing the cursor target to switch back to the menu cursor and therefore hide the gameplay cursor:
https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/1a55d92c719c0d2db2eb0d2c977be242fe2afda8/osu.Game/Graphics/Cursor/MenuCursorContainer.cs#L61-L78

My current fix is to basically early-return in this method if `host.Window.CursorInWindow` became false, but will see if I can fix it more elegantly at a gameplay level.

Looking back at this, not making the gameplay cursor hide when focus lost doesn't seem like a simple thing to do, as the cursor can potentially be in a place where menu cursor could take over (like hold-for-menu button), and therefore cause a resume overlay to appear in that place. 

I'm all in favour of just making the pause instant on focus lost, I can't see any reason why it's delayed to begin with, and just feels incorrect to try fixing this issue by not updating `LastFrameState` on focus lost, instead of never letting gameplay continue.

Being able to potentially delay pause was something we wanted to have around as a gameplay balance measure (to help discourage pausing), but as we now have the setting to adjust the length that is less of a concern.
As a player, it feels really weird when it does not pause immediately upon losing focus.

review_comments: Why is the "replay loaded" check gone now? I don't recall requesting removing it.
It's not something to care about anymore given that this calls `Pause()` directly instead of `performUserRequestedExit()` previously (where if a replay is loaded it'll exit from player immediately)
Half an answer again... "`canPause` inside of `Pause()` checks `HasReplayLoaded` anyway" is the actual complete answer.
I've put it in the description thought you would read it, but sure will try answer completely next time.
